scope: Source review, minimal descendant-lifetime hardening, and40pure mocked monitor checks; no scientific worker or simulation.

findings.issue: Original monitor removed leaders after poll without terminating/reaping surviving same-group descendants; compiler subprocesses can occur via src/life/build.py:71.
findings.resolution: Use the reviewed V pattern: Linux child subreaper, owned-process-group live CPU, unconditional bounded group kill/reap before dropping leaders, and fail-closed cleanup_error records.
findings.post_change_independent_source_review: Root reviewed groupCPU/subreaper/cleanup_group-before-removal/cleanup-error behavior and reported it looked good.

operational_limits: The shared CPU cutoff uses one-second polling and a20CPU-second shutdown margin; RLIMIT_CPU separately limits each worker.
Owned groups are always killed/reaped even when the leader has already exited; cleanup includes adopted descendant CPU before checking the next phase.
A group still present after the bounded teardown produces monitor_failed with cleanup_error and unresolved running identities; no automatic restart or confirmation follows.
This covers reviewed workers and compiler descendants inheriting their process group, not deliberately daemonized processes that escape the owned group.
Pure mocked checks do not establish future host process exit; readiness records exact identities/groups for later host-level clearance.
